# CRDs shipped with the `llm-gateway-apikey` chart

This directory contains every CustomResourceDefinition the chart needs to
install cleanly. Helm processes files under `crds/` **before** any templates
render, and never upgrades or deletes them — so it is the right place for
CRDs that must exist before the chart's other resources are created.

## `kaito.sh_apikeys.yaml` — the APIKey CRD (canonical source)

`kaito.sh_apikeys.yaml` is the **single canonical copy** of the `APIKey`
(`apikeys.kaito.sh`) CustomResourceDefinition for this project.

**Do not edit this file by hand.** It is regenerated by:

```sh
make manifests
```

which runs `controller-gen` against `api/v1alpha1/` and writes the result
directly into this directory. To change the CRD schema, edit the Go types
in `api/v1alpha1/` and re-run `make manifests`, then commit the result.

The filename `kaito.sh_apikeys.yaml` follows controller-gen's
`{group}_{plural}.yaml` naming convention.

### Schema upgrades on existing clusters

Helm's `crds/` directory is **create-only**: `helm upgrade` never updates a
CRD that already exists. When the schema changes (new fields, new
validation rules), you must apply the new CRD manually before upgrading:

```sh
kubectl apply -f chart/llm-gateway-apikey/crds/kaito.sh_apikeys.yaml
helm upgrade llm-gateway-apikey chart/llm-gateway-apikey -n llm-gateway
```

### Migrating from chart versions that managed the CRD via `templates/`

Earlier chart versions installed the CRD from `templates/crd.yaml` (gated
by `crds.install=true`). In those installs the CRD is part of the Helm
release manifest. When you upgrade to a version that has moved the CRD to
`crds/`, Helm will see the template is gone and will try to delete the
CRD — which fails if any `APIKey` resources exist.

**Before** running `helm upgrade`, detach the CRD from the release:

```sh
kubectl annotate crd apikeys.kaito.sh helm.sh/resource-policy=keep
```

After this annotation, Helm leaves the CRD alone and the upgrade succeeds.

# Istio CRDs (temporary)

This directory also ships Istio CRDs bundled with the `llm-gateway-apikey`
chart so that the `EnvoyFilter` (networking.istio.io/v1alpha3) and
`PeerAuthentication` (security.istio.io/v1) templates under
`chart/llm-gateway-apikey/templates/istio/` can apply cleanly on AKS
clusters that use the **Azure AKS application routing add-on**.

## Why is this here?

The AKS app routing add-on installs and manages Istio under the hood,
but it does **not** currently install the full set of Istio CRDs that
arbitrary user workloads may need — in particular, `EnvoyFilter` and
`PeerAuthentication` are not always present out of
the box. Without these CRDs, `helm install` of `llm-gateway-apikey`
fails because the chart's templates reference Kinds the API server
does not know about.

To keep the chart self-contained and installable on app-routing-enabled
clusters, we vendor the CRDs here. Helm installs files under `crds/`
before any templates and never upgrades or deletes them, so this is
safe to ship alongside a managed Istio control plane.

## When can this be removed?

Delete the Istio CRD files once the Azure AKS application routing add-on
installs the required Istio CRDs (`EnvoyFilter`, `PeerAuthentication`,
and anything else `llm-gateway-apikey` templates
depend on) by default. At that point the managed control plane will own the
CRD lifecycle and shipping our own copies risks version drift.

## Source

The Istio CRDs were extracted verbatim from upstream Istio's
`manifests/charts/base/files/crd-all.gen.yaml` (release-1.28). The
upstream `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` annotation is preserved so
that uninstalling `llm-gateway-apikey` does not remove CRDs that other
workloads may rely on.
